You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From ecb6237fa397b7b810d798ad19322eca466dbab1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jun 2022 11:30:37 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] x86/xen: Remove undefined behavior in setup_features()

1 << 31 is undefined. So switch to 1U << 31.

Fixes: 5ead97c84fa7 ("xen: Core Xen implementation")
Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Reviewed-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220617103037.57828-1-julien@xen.org
Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>

diff --git a/drivers/xen/features.c b/drivers/xen/features.c
index 7b591443833c..87f1828d40d5 100644
--- a/drivers/xen/features.c
+++ b/drivers/xen/features.c
@@ -42,7 +42,7 @@ void xen_setup_features(void)
 		if (HYPERVISOR_xen_version(XENVER_get_features, &fi) < 0)
 			break;
 		for (j = 0; j < 32; j++)
-			xen_features[i * 32 + j] = !!(fi.submap & 1<<j);
+			xen_features[i * 32 + j] = !!(fi.submap & 1U << j);
 	}
 
 	if (xen_pv_domain()) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/xen/features.c`**
- The line of code that previously used `1 << j` has been modified to `1U << j`. This change ensures that the left shift operation does not result in undefined behavior by explicitly using an unsigned integer.

### Relationships
- The modification in `drivers/xen/features.c` addresses a potential issue identified in the code where shifting a signed integer could lead to undefined behavior, particularly when the shift exceeds the bit-width of the integer type. By changing `1` to `1U`, the code now correctly uses an unsigned integer, thus preventing any undefined behavior. This change is part of a bug fix related to the core Xen implementation, as indicated by the fix reference in the patch.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
1 << j
```
Reason:
The expression `1 << j` uses a signed integer (1) in a left shift operation. When `j` is 31 or greater on a 32-bit signed integer, it results in undefined behavior due to shifting beyond the bit-width of the integer type.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
1U << j
```
Reason:
Changing the expression to `1U << j` uses an unsigned integer (1U), which prevents undefined behavior when shifting, even if `j` is 31 or more, as unsigned integers can safely accommodate shifts that reach the maximum bit-width.
